items.title: Missed spots
items.short: "2 look clickable, but Tab skips them." Red boxes mark them.
items.long: A red box marks something that looks clickable, like a box with a pointer cursor, a button role or a click handler in the HTML. The keyboard never gets there.

items.title: Hover menus
items.short: "1 menu or box opens only on mouse hover."
items.long: A menu that opens on mouse hover but never when Tab reaches it hides its links from keyboard users. Tab trail reads the page's CSS and marks each one with a red box.

items.title: Forced order
items.short: "1 stop has tabindex above 0, which pulls it ahead of the page."
items.long: An element with tabindex="5" gets Tab before the rest of the page, wherever it sits. When that changes the order, it is listed in red: set it to 0 and move the element in the HTML instead. If it was first anyway, the Log only notes it.

items.title: Hidden focus
items.short: "1 stop is hidden when Tab reaches it." Under a sticky bar.
items.long: When Tab lands on something a sticky header, a cookie bar or a chat button covers completely, the panel lists it in red. Click it to scroll it into view. Fix it and Tab there again: it leaves the list. This check is new in WCAG 2.2 AA.

items.title: Keyboard trap
items.short: "1 stop where Tab gets stuck."
items.long: When Tab and Shift+Tab both leave focus on the same spot, a keyboard user can't get out. The panel lists that stop in red, once, like "2: Message". A spot that keeps Tab but says how to leave, like a code editor, is not red.

items.title: Lost focus
items.short: "1 popup loses focus when it closes."
items.long: When a popup or cookie bar closes, focus should go back to the button that opened it. If it drops to the top of the page instead, the panel lists it in red, like "2 → Start".

items.title: Out of order
items.short: "1 time Tab jumped out of order."
items.long: Each time Tab jumps out of order, the panel lists the jump in red. A popup that blocks the page must get Tab first, or it is flagged too.

items.title: Tab order
items.short: Numbers show where Tab goes. The orange one is where you are.
items.long: Each dot is 1 press of the Tab key, in the order the keyboard visits, and the one you are on turns orange. A line that jumps all over the page will confuse people.

items.title: Hidden links
items.short: Skip links show as dashed dots.
items.long: Some links stay hidden until Tab reaches them, like "Skip to content". They get a dashed dot in the top left corner.

items.title: Inside dialogs
items.short: A dialog opens? The trail goes in too.
items.long: When a page opens a modal dialog (the HTML <dialog> element), the trail goes in too and shows only the stops there. Close it and the page comes back.

items.title: Late arrivals
items.short: Scroll, and new buttons get counted.
items.long: It checks again as you scroll. Buttons that only appear later, like a back to top arrow, get counted too.

items.title: Big pages
items.short: Over 50 stops? See 50 at a time.
items.long: Over 50 stops, it shows 50 at a time. Next and Previous page through them, and Tab turns the page for you. Untick Show 50 stops at a time to see them all.

items.title: Copy for AI
items.short: Paste the problems into your AI. It gets the fix.
items.long: Copies only the problems, each with its WCAG rule, a CSS selector, the HTML, the component and a fix hint. Paste it into your coding AI and it knows where to look.

items.title: Out of the way
items.short: Drag the panel anywhere, or send it to a corner.
items.long: Grab the panel and drag it anywhere, or press the corner button to move it to the next corner. It only moves by itself to stay on screen when it grows, and Compact view under Settings keeps it small.

items.title: Play it
items.short: No Tab key? Press Play, it walks every stop.
items.long: Play moves focus through every stop for you and checks each one, then 1 line sums up all 7 checks. It only moves focus, it never clicks.

items.title: The count
items.short: Fix it, run it again, compare.
items.long: The panel counts the stops and the spots Tab skips. Fix something, run it again and compare the numbers.

items.title: Find it
items.short: Click a red spot in the list to see it.
items.long: The panel lists every spot Tab never reaches, named by its label or text, 50 at a time. Click one and the page scrolls to it and outlines it.

items.title: Log
items.short: See every check, the good ones too.
items.long: Every check as it runs: OK, PROBLEM, SKIPPED with why, or INFO. Filter it, tick Show WCAG to see each rule, click a stop number to jump there, copy it for a bug report, or keep it live in a new tab.

items.title: Keyboard
items.short: No mouse? Ctrl+Shift+F jumps into the panel.
items.long: Press Ctrl+Shift+F, on a Mac and on Windows, and focus jumps to Play in the panel, where Tab reaches every button. Escape takes you back to the stop you were on.

items.title: Jump there
items.short: Click a number and focus moves there.
items.long: Click any number and focus moves to that spot, as if you had tabbed there. The next Tab goes on from it, and it is not counted as a jump.

items.title: Spotlight
items.short: Dim the page, light up where Tab is.
items.long: Open Settings and tick Spotlight: the page goes dark except what Tab is on, so you follow it the way a keyboard user does. A missing focus ring is easy to spot, even for someone watching.

items.title: Show lines
items.short: Just the numbers? Untick Show lines.
items.long: Open Settings and untick Show lines, and only the numbered dots stay. Long lines turns grey until you tick Show lines again.

items.title: Long lines
items.short: Too many lines? Untick Long lines.
items.long: Open Settings, untick Long lines, and no line is over 100 px. A longer one becomes 2 arrows, 1 from each stop. A line off screen becomes 1 arrow pointing its way.

items.title: Out of Tab
items.short: The panel stays out of the trail.
items.long: Leave this panel out of Tab is ticked at first, so Tab never runs into the panel. Untick it and Tab reaches the panel's buttons too. Ctrl+Shift+F gets you in either way.
